newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended down but off earlier lows on Friday as some investors cashed out profits in blue chips ahead of the weekend, brokers said.
But sustained buying interest in several counters following their inclusion in the new Morgan Stanley Capital Index (MSCI) prevented the index from a sharp decline, they said.
"The fact that some investors bought back fundamentally sound Gudang Garam also helped the index to slightly recover from earlier lows," one broker said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 2.56 points, or 0.39 percent, to close at 647.89 points after touching a low of 644.53 points.
Decliners led advancers by 62 to 49, with 68 counters unchanged. Total turnover was estimated at about 378 billion rupiah.
A broker with a London-based securities house said investors bought back Gudang Garam and Indocement because they were oversold on Thursday after MSCI announced its new index.
MSCI had downgraded the wieghting of Gudang Garam and deleted Indocement from the index.
Blue chips including Bank Negara Indonesia, Bimantara Citra and Semen Gresik were a target of profit takers, brokers said.
The stocks made significants gains on Thursday after their inclusion in the MSCI.
On Friday, BNI was the most active stock, falling 50 rupiah to 1,450 rupiah, with some 22.8 million shares traded.
Paper and pulp maker Indah Kiat gained 100 rupiah to 2,025 on a volume of 1.83 million shares on what brokers said was due to market talk of a possible rights issue.

Medium-sized Bank Tiara fell 25 rupiah to 2,925 on a volume of 153,000 shares on profit-taking although it announced a net profit of 15.01 billion rupiah in 1997's first quarter against 83.1 billion rupiah in the year-ago period.
"The results were encouraging but I recommend a "hold" for a short term because the upside level for the stock is limited," said Mirza Adityaswara, an analyst at BZW Niaga Securities.
He said the stock currently was traded at around 9.5 times 1997 earnings. "This is quite expensive for medium-sized banking stocks," Adityaswara added.
